## Analysis code for results relating to Figure 2 

```{r display-settings, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = FALSE)
```

## Inputs

- `data/MAI_prot_model_new.rds`: processed SummarizedExperiment from protein_matrix_QC,
  containing the log2-scaled unimputed and `MAI_imputed` assay and protein/run metadata.
  
- `data/merged_markers_filtered.csv`: the final curated marker set. 

- The original `demogs` dataset contains `Subject`, `Group`(CON/RES/AD/DEM), `age_death`, `pmi`, `study`, and `msex` and is external to this analysis*. Instead, use the subject_group.csv file provided to map subject to disease group, which only contains disease category (CON/RES/AD/DEM).

-  `prop_long` object is derived using the above to generate marker profiles
  
*Subject-level inputs and generated objects are not distributed with the public
code. ROSMAP participant-level clinical and neuropathological data can be requested through the Rush Alzheimer’s Disease Center at https://www.radc.rush.edu and AD Knowledge Portal at https://www.synapse.org, subject to the applicable data-use agreements. 


## Prepare protein intensities and subject-normalised profiles


```{r prepare-profiles}
library(SummarizedExperiment)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(tibble)
library(purrr)

data_dir <- "path/to/directory"

# Load the processed protein matrix.
se_log2_07 <- readRDS(file.path(data_dir, "MAI_prot_model_new.rds"))
se_log2_07 #summarizedExperiment, with global filter of <0.7 missingness, unimputed and MAI_imputed stored here (both log-scaled)

# 2) Extract the imputed assay data and back-transform 
# - Imputed matrix is used

MAI_raw <- 2^(assay(se_log2_07, "MAI_imputed")) %>% #log-scaled currently, so back-transform to raw-intensities
  as.data.frame() %>% #convert to dataframe
  rownames_to_column("feature_id") %>% #set proteins as a column
  pivot_longer(-feature_id, names_to = "SampleID", values_to = "value") #pivot long

# 3) extract row/col metadata from summarizedExperiment
rd <- rowData(se_log2_07) %>% as.data.frame() %>% rownames_to_column("feature_id") #protein metadata
cd <- colData(se_log2_07) %>% as.data.frame() %>% rownames_to_column("SampleID") #sample metadata

# sample-category (this ONLY includes disease status for subjects)
demogs <- readr::read_csv(file.path(data_dir, "subject_group.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)

# 4) Join metadata to assay
long <- MAI_raw %>% #join long assays with row data
  left_join(rd, by = "feature_id") %>%
  left_join(cd, by = "SampleID") %>%
  left_join(demogs %>% select(Subject, Group), by = "Subject")

glimpse(long) #check result

#sum normalise
prop <- long %>%
  mutate(log2Quant = log2(value)) %>%
  group_by(Subject, feature_id) %>%
  mutate(sum = sum(value, na.rm = TRUE),
         prop = value / sum) %>%
  ungroup()
```


## Figure 2A: Mean profiles and Ward D2 clustering

Subject-protein intensities are sum-normalised, then the cohort-mean profile is derived. 
Each mean protein profile is row-z-scaled. Euclidean distance and Ward's D2 clustering are used, 
with the dendrogram cut at k=15 clusters. 

```{r ward-clustering-and-heatmap}
library(tibble)
library(ggplot2)

#1) generate mean matrix (the cohort mean of protein fractionation profiles) 
prot_frac_mean <- prop %>%
  mutate(Fraction = factor(Fraction, levels = c("1","2","3","4","5","6","7"))) %>% #order
  group_by(feature_id, Fraction) %>% #group by protein-fraction
  summarise(mean_prop = mean(prop, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

#2) pivot wide: proteins × fractions
prop_mat <- prot_frac_mean %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = Fraction, values_from = mean_prop) %>%
  arrange(feature_id) %>%
  column_to_rownames("feature_id") %>% # proteins as rownames, fractions as columns
  as.matrix() #mean proportional protein matrix

#3) z-score rows (each protein across fractions). 
prot_z <- t(scale(t(prop_mat)))  # mean=0, sd=1 per protein

#4) Hierarchical clustering of profiles, K = 15
d <- dist(prot_z) 
hc <- hclust(d, method = "ward.D2")
clusters <- cutree(hc, k = 15)

#5) save as dataframe
cluster_df <- tibble(feature_id = rownames(prot_z), cluster = factor(sprintf("%02d", clusters)))
cluster_df %>% group_by(cluster) %>% summarise(n = n(), .groups = "drop") #summary

#6) make heatmap
cluster_df <- cluster_df[match(rownames(prot_z), cluster_df$feature_id), ]

# order proteins by cluster in the matrix (so blocks are visible)
prot_z_ord <- prot_z[order(cluster_df$cluster), ]
ann_row <- data.frame(Cluster = cluster_df$cluster[order(cluster_df$cluster)])
rownames(ann_row) <- rownames(prot_z_ord)

library(paletteer)
# z-score heatmap colours (divergent gradient)
heat_cols <- paletteer_c("grDevices::Cork", 30)
cluster_levels <- levels(cluster_df$cluster)
cluster_cols <- paletteer_d("ggthemes::calc", 12) 
#extend 12-colour palette to 15 colours
extra_cols <- c("#D02090","#00CDCD", "#9B30FF") 
cluster_cols <- c(cluster_cols, extra_cols)

cluster_cols <- setNames(cluster_cols, cluster_levels)

library(ComplexHeatmap)
library(circlize)
col_fun <- colorRamp2( #extract colour palette
  seq(min(prot_z_ord, na.rm = TRUE), 
      max(prot_z_ord, na.rm = TRUE), 
      length.out = length(heat_cols)),  heat_cols)
row_ha <- rowAnnotation( #assign colours to clusters
  Cluster = ann_row$Cluster,
  col = list(Cluster = cluster_cols),
  show_annotation_name = FALSE)

#plot heatmap
ht <- Heatmap(
  prot_z_ord,
  name = "z-score",
  col = col_fun,
  cluster_rows = FALSE,
  cluster_columns = FALSE,
  show_row_names = FALSE,
  column_title = "Protein fractionation profile clustering",
  right_annotation = row_ha)

#add legends
draw(ht,
  heatmap_legend_side = "left",
  annotation_legend_side = "left",
  merge_legends = FALSE,
  legend_grouping = "original")
```


## Figure 2A: GO cellular-component enrichment

The background comprises the clustered protein IDs. Original enrichment and
term-selection settings are preserved, including the second BH adjustment over
the returned, fold-enrichment-filtered terms. This is not an adjustment over
all GO tests originally performed. Annotation/package versions are required
for exact reproduction.

**Unresolved plot metric:** the original lollipop code maps `Signal` to the
x-axis while labelling it "Strength". `Strength = log10(FoldEnrichment)`;
`Signal` combines Strength with adjusted significance. The source expression
is retained here pending confirmation of which metric generated Figure 2A.


```{r go-enrichment}
## Extract uniprot codes for GO analysis
uniprot_codes <- rd %>% dplyr::select(Genes, Protein.Group) %>% distinct() %>% 
  rename(feature_id = Protein.Group)
#cluster_df <- cluster_df %>% left_join(uniprot_codes, by = c("feature_id"))

## generate background set
bg_uniprot <- cluster_df %>% filter(!is.na(feature_id)) %>% pull(feature_id) %>% unique()

## 3) Split UniProt IDs by cluster (generate cluster input sets)
cluster_genes <- cluster_df %>% 
  left_join(uniprot_codes, by = "feature_id") %>%
  filter(!is.na(feature_id)) %>%
  group_by(cluster) %>% reframe(feature_id = unique(feature_id)) %>%
  split(.$cluster) %>% lapply(\(df) df$feature_id)

### GO:CC
library(clusterProfiler)
library(org.Hs.eg.db) #homo sapiens

ego_list <- lapply(names(cluster_genes), function(clust){ #for each cluster
  # skip small clusters
  if (length(cluster_genes[[clust]]) < 20) return(NULL)
  
 ego <- enrichGO( #make this table
    gene          = cluster_genes[[clust]], #the genes in the cluster
    universe      = bg_uniprot,   #background universe = all unique proteins in matrix
    OrgDb         = org.Hs.eg.db,   #organism database
    keyType       = "UNIPROT",    #Uniprot IDs
    ont           = "CC",  #cell component (GO:CC sets)
    pAdjustMethod = "BH",   #benj-hoch FDR adjustment
    qvalueCutoff  = 0.05,    #q-value cutoff
    readable      = TRUE)
  
  #If there are no enriched terms for this cluster, return NULL
  if (is.null(ego) || nrow(as.data.frame(ego)) == 0) return(NULL)
  
  df <- as.data.frame(ego)      # <-- this pulls out the table you printed
  df$cluster <- clust #add cluster ID
  df 
})
```

- Function to extract GO terms
```{r select-go-terms}
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)
library(stringr)

top_terms <- function(ego_list, n_terms , fdr_thresh , FE_min , Count_thresh ) {
  ### arguments = GO cluster list, number of terms to select, FDR threshold, min fold enrich, min members

  go_all <- purrr::list_rbind(ego_list) %>% #combine all clusters into one dataframe
    
    #record cluster metadata
    mutate(cluster = sprintf("%02d", as.integer(cluster)),
      Count = as.integer(Count), #number of entries
      pvalue = as.numeric(pvalue),
      FoldEnrichment = as.numeric(FoldEnrichment)) %>%
    #filter for fold enrichment (FE_min) above threshold argument
    filter(!is.na(pvalue), !is.na(FoldEnrichment), FoldEnrichment > FE_min) %>%
    
    #calculate global FDR (all combined clusters) and strength
    mutate(FDR_global = p.adjust(pvalue, method = "BH"),
      FDR_global = pmax(FDR_global, .Machine$double.xmin),
      ScaledFE = log10(FoldEnrichment), 
      FDR_term = -log10(FDR_global),
      #harmonic mean prioritises terms with both strong enrichment and statistical support
      Strength = 2 * ScaledFE * FDR_term / (ScaledFE + FDR_term)) %>% 
    #then filter according to arguments
    filter(FDR_global < fdr_thresh, Count > Count_thresh) %>%
    
    #make sure no Gene set matches are repeated by keeping the top one
    group_by(geneID) %>% 
    arrange(desc(ScaledFE), .by_group = TRUE) %>% slice_head(n = 1) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    
    #make sure no Descriptions are repeated by keeping the top one
    group_by(Description) %>% 
    arrange(desc(ScaledFE), .by_group = TRUE) %>% slice_head(n = 1) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    
    #Rank by enrichment, count within cluster
    group_by(cluster) %>%
    arrange(desc(ScaledFE), desc(Count), .by_group = TRUE) %>% 
    slice_head(n = n_terms) %>% #take top n terms here in order they'll be shown
    ungroup() %>%
    
    #arrange
    arrange(cluster, desc(ScaledFE), Count) %>%
    relocate(cluster, .before = 1)

  go_all
}
```

### This chunk below extracts the top 2 GO:CC terms per cluster at:
- global FDR < 0.05
- fold enrichment > 1.5
- with at least 20 pathway entries
- the go_top function also removes any redundant descriptions (keeps the strongest)

```{r go-lollipop-plot}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(stringr)
library(ggplot2)
library(forcats)
library(tidytext)

go_top <- top_terms(ego_list, n_terms = 2, fdr_thresh = 0.05, FE_min = 1.5, Count_thresh = 20)

# ---- top 2 largest terms per cluster ----
plot_df <- go_top %>%
  group_by(cluster) %>%
  arrange(desc(Strength), .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    cluster = factor(cluster, levels = sprintf("%02d", 1:15)),
    term = Description,
    term = tidytext::reorder_within(term, Strength, cluster))

# ---- size legend breaks: rounded to nearest 5 across the plotted data ----
min_k <- min(plot_df$Count, na.rm = TRUE)
max_k <- max(plot_df$Count, na.rm = TRUE)
min_k5 <- floor(min_k / 5) * 5
max_k5 <- ceiling(max_k / 5) * 5
size_breaks <- unique(round(seq(min_k5, max_k5, length.out = 5) / 5) * 5)
size_breaks <- size_breaks[size_breaks >= min_k5 & size_breaks <= max_k5]

library(stringr)
plot_df$term <- str_wrap(plot_df$term, width = 50)


# ---- plot ----
ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = Strength, y = term, color = cluster)) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = 0, xend = Strength, yend = term), linewidth = 0.8, alpha = 0.9) +
  geom_point(aes(size = Count), alpha = 0.6) +
  #geom_text(aes(label = formatC(FDR_global, format = "e", digits = 0)), color = "grey20", size = 1, hjust = -0.3, fontface = "bold") +
  facet_wrap(~ cluster, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  tidytext::scale_y_reordered(position = "right") +
  scale_color_manual(values = cluster_cols, guide = "none") +
  scale_size_continuous(
    name   = "count",
    range  = c(1, 7),
    breaks = size_breaks,
    limits = c(min_k5, max_k5)) +
  labs(x = "Strength", y = NULL, title = "GO:CC Strength by cluster") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 13) +
  theme(legend.position = "right", panel.spacing.y = unit(0.2, "lines"),
    plot.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold", colour = "black"),
    strip.background = element_blank(),
    strip.text = element_blank(), 
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 12, face = "italic")) +
  coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
  guides(size = guide_legend(override.aes = list(alpha = 1)))
```


## Marker input

Load the final assignments produced by the separate curation workflow. The
source Rmd also filtered and reassigned entries after loading the CSV; these
steps are intentionally excluded. The input supplied here must already contain
the final assignments used for the figure.


```{r load-markers}
library(readr)
all_markers_final <- read_csv(file.path(data_dir, "merged_markers_filtered.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)

marker_palette <- c(
  "Secretory Pathway"     = "#FFD700",
  "Plasma Membrane"       = "#778B00",
  "Cytosol"               = "#00E2E5",
  "Cytoskeleton"          = "#FF0010",
  "Presynapse"            = "#DEA0FD",
  "Postsynapse"           = "#C8308C",
  "Peroxisome"            = "#6A33C2",
  "Mitochondria"          = "#9DCC00",
  "Nucleus"               = "navy",
  "Ribosome"              = "#0075DC",
  "Proteasome"            = "#8B3B00")

plot_palette <- c(marker_palette, "unknown" = "grey80")
```


## Marker profiles: Supplementary Figure S2

```{r marker-profiles}
final_profiles <- prop %>% 
  inner_join(all_markers_final %>% dplyr::select(Protein.Group, markers) %>% 
               distinct(), by = "Protein.Group") %>%
  mutate(Fraction = factor(Fraction, levels = c("1","2","3","4","5","6","7"))) %>%
  group_by(markers, Protein.Group, Fraction) %>%
  summarise(
    n = sum(!is.na(prop)),
    mean_prop = mean(prop, na.rm = TRUE),
    sdev = sd(prop, na.rm = TRUE),
    sem = sdev / sqrt(n),
    .groups = "drop")

ggplot(final_profiles, #then do the same again for log
  aes(x = Fraction, y = mean_prop, group = Protein.Group, color = markers)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.3, linewidth = 0.7) +
  scale_color_manual(values = marker_palette) +
  labs(title = "Compartment class marker profiles",
       subtitle = "Mean proportional abundance across subjects",
       x = "Fraction", y = "Mean proportional abundance",
       color = "Consensus class") +
  facet_wrap(~markers, ncol = 4, scales = "fixed") +
  theme_classic(base_family = "Helvetica") +
  theme(
    strip.text = element_text(size = 9, face = "bold"), #bold facet labels
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"), #bold title
    legend.position = "none")
```

```{r}
overall_profile <- final_profiles %>%

  summarise(
```

## Figure 2Ciii: t-SNE (input provenance unresolved)



```{r tsne}
#T-sne 
library(Rtsne)

## Optional but recommended:
## scale fractions so t-SNE is not dominated by one fraction.
mat_scaled <- scale(prop_mat)

## ---- 8) Run t-SNE ----
set.seed(3)
tsne_out <- Rtsne(mat_scaled, dims = 2, perplexity = 50, theta = 0.5, pca = TRUE, check_duplicates = FALSE)

## ---- 9) t-SNE coordinates + labels ----
df_tsne <- as.data.frame(tsne_out$Y) %>%
  setNames(c("tSNE1", "tSNE2")) %>% rownames_to_column("Protein.Group")

## Rtsne does not preserve rownames automatically, so add them manually
df_tsne$Protein.Group <- rownames(mat_scaled)

df_tsne <- df_tsne %>%
  left_join(all_markers_final %>% dplyr::select(Protein.Group, markers) %>% 
               distinct(), by = "Protein.Group") %>%
  mutate(label = ifelse(is.na(markers), "unknown", as.character(markers)),
         label = factor(label, levels = c(names(marker_palette), "unknown")))

unknown_alpha <- 0.06
unknown_size  <- 4
known_alpha   <- 0.80
known_size    <- 4

ggplot(df_tsne, aes(x = tSNE1, y = tSNE2)) +
  
  # faint density/context layer for the full unlabelled proteome
  stat_density_2d(
    data = df_tsne %>% filter(label == "unknown"),
    aes(x = tSNE1, y = tSNE2),
    geom = "polygon",
    fill = "grey70",
    colour = NA,
    alpha = 0.04,
    bins = 8) +
  
  #unknown/background proteins
  geom_point(
    data = df_tsne %>% filter(label == "unknown"),
    aes(colour = label),
    alpha = unknown_alpha,
    size = unknown_size) +
  
  #known marker proteins
  geom_point(
    data = df_tsne %>% filter(label != "unknown"),
    aes(fill = label),
    shape = 21,
    colour = "grey20",
    stroke = 0.18,
    alpha = known_alpha,
    size = known_size) +
  
  scale_colour_manual(values = plot_palette, drop = FALSE) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = plot_palette, drop = FALSE) +
  
  theme_classic(base_size = 10, base_family = "Helvetica") +
  labs(title = "t-SNE of protein fractionation profiles",
    subtitle = "Sum-normalised and z-scaled",
    x = "t-SNE 1",
    y = "t-SNE 2",
    colour = "compartment",
    fill = "compartment") +
  theme(legend.position = "right",
    plot.title = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 10),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 10))
```


## Figure 2D: Within-group subject correlations

- Each subject has 7271 protein fractionation profiles (log-scaled, MAI imputed). 
- Pearson correlations are computed separately for CON, RES,and AD-DEM using pairwise complete observations.
- The heatmap diagonal represents self-self correlation
- the violin plot shows the distribution of pairwise correlation by group (one value per unique pair, excludes the diagnoal)

Heatmaps include self-correlations; violin summaries retain one value per
unique pair and exclude self-correlations. The source plotting limits are
preserved. The reported 0.952–0.985 range has not been recomputed here.


```{r correlation-heatmaps}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1) Prepare data
# ------------------------------------------------------------
corr_input <- prop %>%
  mutate(
    Fraction = as.character(Fraction),
    feature_fraction = paste0(feature_id, "_F", Fraction)) %>%
  dplyr::select(Group, Subject, feature_fraction, log2Quant)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2) Function to make subject-subject correlation heatmap
# ------------------------------------------------------------
make_corr_heatmap <- function(df, group_name, show_legend = TRUE) {
  
  wide <- df %>%
    filter(Group == group_name) %>%
    dplyr::select(Subject, feature_fraction, log2Quant) %>%
    pivot_wider(
      names_from = Subject, values_from = log2Quant)
  
  mat <- wide %>%
    dplyr::select(-feature_fraction) %>% as.matrix()
  
  rownames(mat) <- wide$feature_fraction
  
  cor_mat <- cor(mat, use = "pairwise.complete.obs", method = "pearson")
  
  cor_df <- as.data.frame(cor_mat) %>%
    rownames_to_column("Subject1") %>%
    pivot_longer(cols = -Subject1, names_to = "Subject2", values_to = "correlation")
  
  p <- ggplot(cor_df, aes(x = Subject1, y = Subject2, fill = correlation)) +
    geom_tile() +
    scale_fill_viridis_c(
      option = "mako", direction = -1,
      limits = c(0.95, 1),
      name = "Pearson's r") +
    labs(title = "", subtitle = group_name,
      x = NULL, y = NULL) +
    theme_classic(base_family = "Helvetica") +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14, hjust = 0.5),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 12),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 12),
      axis.text.x = element_blank(),
      axis.text.y = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks = element_blank())
  
  # toggle legend
  if (!show_legend) {
    p <- p + theme(legend.position = "none")
  }
  
  return(p)
}

p_con <- make_corr_heatmap(corr_input, "CON", show_legend = FALSE)
p_ad  <- make_corr_heatmap(corr_input, "AD-DEM", show_legend = FALSE)
p_res <- make_corr_heatmap(corr_input, "RES", show_legend = TRUE)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Extract pairwise correlations per group
# ------------------------------------------------------------
get_pairwise_corrs <- function(df, group_name) {
  
  wide <- df %>%
    filter(Group == group_name) %>%
    dplyr::select(Subject, feature_fraction, log2Quant) %>%
    pivot_wider(
      names_from = Subject,
      values_from = log2Quant)
  
  mat <- wide %>%
    dplyr::select(-feature_fraction) %>% as.matrix()
  
  rownames(mat) <- wide$feature_fraction
  
  cor_mat <- cor(mat, use = "pairwise.complete.obs", method = "pearson")
  
  as.data.frame(cor_mat) %>%
    rownames_to_column("Subject1") %>%
    pivot_longer(
      cols = -Subject1,
      names_to = "Subject2",
      values_to = "correlation") %>%
    filter(Subject1 < Subject2) %>%   #upper triangle only
    mutate(Group = group_name)
}

corr_dist <- bind_rows(
  get_pairwise_corrs(corr_input, "CON"),
  get_pairwise_corrs(corr_input, "RES"),
  get_pairwise_corrs(corr_input, "AD-DEM"))

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Summary stats if you want to report them
# ------------------------------------------------------------
corr_dist %>%
  group_by(Group) %>%
  summarise(min = min(correlation), max = max(correlation),
    median_r = median(correlation, na.rm = TRUE),
    q1 = quantile(correlation, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
    q3 = quantile(correlation, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

group_palette <- c("CON" = "royalblue1", "RES" = "yellowgreen", "AD-DEM" = "indianred2")

corr_dist_plot <- ggplot(corr_dist, aes(x = Group, y = correlation, fill = Group)) +
  geom_violin(trim = TRUE, width = 0.85, alpha = 0.8, colour = NA) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.14, outlier.shape = NA, fill = "white", colour = "grey25", alpha = 0.5) +
  stat_summary(fun = median, geom = "point",
    size = 2,
    colour = "black") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = group_palette) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0.84, 1)) +
  labs(title = "Pairwise subject profile correlation", subtitle = "Median and IQR",
    x = NULL, y = "Pairwise Pearson's r") +
  theme_classic(base_family = "Helvetica") +
  theme(legend.position = "none",
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 12),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 12))

corr_dist_plot | p_ad | p_con | p_res
```
